mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Federal Funds Rate turns negative (i.e., rate cuts), the discount rate for future cash flows falls, lowering the present value of expected dividends and equity prices, which drives a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during confirmed rate-cut periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) creates expectations of sustained wage growth and economic expansion, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month > previous 3 months by > 2% AND HOUST month > previous 3 months by > 5%
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day ahead returns show no significant correlation with the combined labor indicators (Pearson IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in retail sales (GDPC1) above 2% suggests resilient consumer demand, which lowers risk premiums and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite persistent monthly GDPC1 growth above 2% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month average accompanied by a sharp drop in inflation (CPIAUCSL), signals supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month < 12-month average AND CPIAUCSL month > 12-month average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained supply contraction (IC > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform due to risk aversion, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns regardless of other macro signals.
failure_condition: In high-unemployment regimes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: if RSAFS rises > 10% in a month, it implies labor market loosening that supports equity valuations, predicting positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant relationship with the RSAFS spike (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indexes (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3% suggest accelerating inflation, which raises policy uncertainty and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during such inflation spikes (IC > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (GDPC1) both fall sequentially by more than 5% in the same month, it indicates simultaneous supply and demand pressures that depress market sentiment and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month < previous month by > 5% AND GDPC1 month < previous month by > 5%
regime_hint: dual contraction in output and demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite simultaneous >5% declines in both INDPRO and GDPC1 (IC > 0.15).
